events.label: Bessent 'Operation Economic Fury' press conference — Iran economic isolation plan details
events.note: Updated Aug 24 morning: Brent pulled back to $93.09 (-1.38%) ahead of the press conference after closing at $94.39 Friday (formal $94 trigger breached). Iran's national security chief threatened Hormuz ship seizures; Pezeshkian's de-escalation signal ('cannot continue with war forever') provides the diplomatic off-ramp. Six vessels transited the strait in the prior 24 hours — threat not yet enforcement. Resolution: comprehensive secondary sanctions (any Iran oil buyer faces US financial exclusion) returns Brent above $94 and re-activates the regime trigger through NVDA's Aug 26 print; targeted sanctions keeps Brent in $91–93 and leaves the path constructive; diplomatic framing plus Pezeshkian channel deactivates the trigger.

events.label: US-Canada 50% tariffs effective — $28B of Canadian goods; Canada retaliates Sept 8
events.note: Added Aug 24 morning: Trade talks collapsed Friday night after Trump declared a deal at 4PM; 50% tariffs on $28B of Canadian wine, cement, lumber, and electronics took effect at midnight. PM Carney: Canada will match 'dollar for dollar' effective Sept 8, targeting dairy, appliances, agricultural equipment, pulp and paper, and electronics. Manufacturing PMI already showed supply-chain stress at a 13-month high on Friday. Canada's retaliatory tariffs arrive 8 days before the Sept 16 FOMC — if Warsh at Jackson Hole (Aug 28) cites this as an inflation risk on top of Iran oil pressure, September hike odds above the current 31% would increase.

events.label: NVDA Q2 FY27 earnings (est.) — Brent regime trigger now active entering print
events.note: Updated Aug 24 morning: Brent at $93.09 (pulled back from $94.39 Friday breach); 30Y at 5.28% (2bps from 5.30% trigger). AMD at $462–478, seven sessions below $484 containment — two sessions remaining before print. ROST $239.67 Friday close — held $235 floor, no gap-and-fade. US-Canada 50% tariffs effective midnight add cost-push on top of oil pressure. Bessent press conference today resolves the Brent direction. Consensus: revenue $91.85B vs $91.0B guidance midpoint, GAAP GM 74.9%, EPS $2.08; Q3 FY27 forward guide is the market-moving number. Jackson Hole begins Aug 27 — no de-risk window between the print and Warsh's keynote.

events.label: Jackson Hole Economic Policy Symposium (Aug 27–29) — Warsh keynote Aug 28; Brent regime trigger now active
events.note: Updated Aug 24 morning: Brent at $93.09 (pulled back from $94.39 Friday breach but trigger remains active). 30Y at 5.28%, 2bps from 5.30% trigger. US-Canada 50% tariffs effective midnight add cost-push inflation signal ahead of Warsh's keynote. September hike odds 31% — bifurcated PMI (services 56.8, 4-year high; manufacturing 53.2 miss), Canada tariff escalation, and Iran oil pressure make the September 16 FOMC path highly uncertain. Warsh's Aug 28 keynote (first as Fed Chair) is the key event: does he frame Brent above $90 as transitory (hold) or a sustained supply constraint (higher-for-longer)? With Canada tariffs now live, the dual inflation question (energy + tariffs) is the framing test. NVDA prints Aug 26 AH — one day before Jackson Hole opens, no de-risk gap. UMich final (Aug 28) is a within-symposium data point; prior: 51.0 (multi-year low).

events.label: Canada retaliatory tariffs effective — dairy, appliances, ag equipment, pulp, paper, electronics
events.note: Added Aug 24 morning: Response to US 50% tariffs on $28B of Canadian goods (effective Aug 24). PM Carney: 'Canada will match those tariffs dollar for dollar.' Targeted sectors: dairy, appliances, agricultural equipment, pulp and paper, electronics. Arrives 8 days before the Sept 16 FOMC — if Warsh at Jackson Hole (Aug 28) cites Canada-US tariff escalation as an inflation risk on top of Iran oil pressure, September hike odds above 31% would increase. Manufacturing supply-chain stress was already at a 13-month high on Friday's PMI.

events.label: AVGO Q3 FY2026 earnings (est.) — through $380 structural support; VMware + AI concentration dual overhang
events.note: Updated Aug 19 night: AVGO fell 5% to ~$362 on August 19, breaking through $380 structural support. VMware CVE-2026-59310 active exploitation (361 IPs, 47 countries per Aug 14 disclosure) + 72% AI revenue concentration (~72% of next-quarter sequential growth) create dual overhang. At ~65x trailing P/E, any miss or margin compression compounds. Q3 FY2026 results (est. September 4–5) are the first public accounting of both: VMware remediation costs in financial guidance, enterprise customer commentary on the incident, and AI revenue breadth. $380 is now resistance; $340–350 is the next structured support zone. Flip: recovery above $380 on volume, or formal VMware incident-containment statement before earnings.

events.label: Bessent Treasury long-dated buyback ops begin — $4B+ per op, 10-20yr and 20-30yr bonds
events.note: Added Aug 19 night: Treasury Secretary Bessent announced August 19 the department will double the size of long-dated bond buyback operations, raising the maximum per-operation from $2B to at least $4B for bonds maturing in the 10-to-20-year and 20-to-30-year ranges. Effective September 9, runs through November 4 (end of current refunding quarter). Immediate market impact: 30Y fell 9bps to 5.196% on the announcement. The program provides structural demand support for the long end through the NVDA print (Aug 26), Jackson Hole (Aug 27–29), and into October. If underlying supply dynamics ($432B July deficit, $1.7T corporate issuance) overwhelm the $4B+ buyback, the 30Y could reassert above 5.25% before the program begins.

events.label: SPCX 180-day IPO lock-up expiry (approx.) — terminal insider/early-investor float unlock
events.note: ~180 days after the June 12 debut. Lock-up expiries are the known supply overhang for hot IPOs. Context after Aug 6-7: 20% first tranche absorbed at $105-$115; next tranches scheduled Aug 20 and late September. Q3 Starlink profitability (~October call) is the only fundamental catalyst that could revalue the lockup discount before the December terminal release. SPCX Q2: $18.37B capex vs $7.81B revenue; AI segment $2.56B (+247% YoY).

events.label: OpenAI IPO — target window H1 2027 after 2026 delay
events.note: OpenAI delayed its anticipated 2026 IPO to H1 2027 (announced June 26, 2026). PLTR's 149% US commercial growth, AMD's $6.7B data-center (+107%), and SpaceX's exclusive Nvidia commitment ($15.83B AI capex) confirm the enterprise AI adoption underlying OpenAI's revenue model. NVDA circular financing disclosure ($250B OpenAI backstop) remains the unresolved structural question that may surface in S-1 filings.
